quest.title: The Phaethons' Syrtos
quest.description: You help Clymene pay respects at seven royal tombs to lay the souls of the Sunchildren to rest...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.text: Hmm? How strange. I have not seen someone in your garb for a many long years...
From your mannerisms, you are not from Byakuyakoku either.
Are you some guest from afar who fell into this place?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's more or less correct...
To think that there were ways to access Byakuyakoku from the outside world... Shocking news indeed.
I was born here, and I have never seen anyone from the outside world.
Someone once told me that he wanted to catch a glimpse of the world outside. I took his words for a jest...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: *sigh*
Traveler. In truth, I have a humble request for you.
There are seven royal tombs scattered throughout Byakuyakoku, in which the remains of our "Sunchi{RUBY#[S]Phaethons}ldren" have been interred.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Sunchildren...
Indeed. Here, we worship the Dainichi Mikoshi.
After a certain number of years, an infant will be chosen as the Sunchild, gaining control over the nation.
We had... a total of seven Sunchildren.
O rare Traveler from another land, please, kindly pay respects at their tombs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, why would you need us outsiders to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't it usually up to their family and friends to pay respects to them?
Indeed, that would normally be the case.
Unfortunately, I fear that no one in this nation would want to do so.
In fact, it is likely that these royal tombs have not been visited in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do the people of this nation dislike the Sunchildren?
"Dislike" is perhaps too kind a word. "Detest" might be more fitting.
As I said earlier, the Sunchildren were born into their role.
But how could mere children rule a nation? The ones who truly controlled everything were powerful people behind the scenes.
The Sunchildren were mere puppets, their every move manipulated by these people.
And yet there was no end to the greed of those powerful people. They grew fat off the toil of the people, compelling the Sunchildren to perform heinous deeds.
And so, the peoples' ire rose, and many of those sins were laid at the feet of the Sunchildren.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's awful...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Sunchildren were innocent!
Innocent? Oh no, they were not.
As far as the people of Byakuyakoku were concerned, their ignorance was the greatest sin of all.
A sin, even committed in ignorance, can hurt others. Can a person who commits such transgressions truly be called innocent?
It would be difficult, no? The damage is already done, and it cannot be undone.

choices.text: But if that's what you think...

response.text: Well, you can consider this... my personal sentimentality speaking.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: My name is Clymene. I was a female official in charge of taking care of the Sunchildren's daily lives within the Dainichi Mikoshi.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Though I knew that they did wrong, and though I was aware that they were being manipulated...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: They were still children that I watched grow up. I pitied them, and I grieved for them...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: In the end, I could not hate them...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Though my work involved being around them every day, I was under heavy surveillance.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: I was not permitted to say a single word when I was around those children.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: But when no one was around, when they were helpless and afraid, they would say so, so many things to me...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: ...And I could not offer them a single word in reply.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: If I had possessed but a little self-sacrificial courage to say something, anything to them...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Perhaps everything might have gone differently...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: So please, I beg you. I cannot face them as I am, so this is the only way I can honor them.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Please, good Traveler, lend me your aid just this once.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: A single Sango Pearl is all I ask, to be laid before their tombs.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: This way, you'll be able to light the Soul Lamps at the stone shrine here and open the way to the Soul Guide's Locus and bring their spirits peace...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Thank you. This task is in your hands, then.

choices.text: Why do you still want us to pay our respects to them?

talks.objective: Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: There were seven Sunchildren in all. Traveler, please take my place and pay respects before their tombs.

talks.objective: Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Ah, the seven Soul Lamps are lit...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: It seems that you have completed your task. I will always remember how you have aided me.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Now come, allow me to open it for you... The path to the Soul Guide's Locus.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Traveler from a foreign land, I know that I have caused you much trouble... But please, bear witness as they are laid to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Follow this path. I will meet you on its far side.

talks.objective: Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Ah, Traveler, you have arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: This is the Soul Guide's Locus, and this is where my final thoughts remain.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: When the Sunchildren reached a certain age, they would follow a ceremony and enter the Dainichi Mikoshi on their birth date.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Yes, and that process was known as the Rite of Solar Return.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: The Sunchildren were birthed from the Dainichi Mikoshi, and they would again return to the seat of the sun before the mortal world could taint them.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: ...The temperature of the Dainichi Mikoshi was such that its light could warm all of Byakuyakoku.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Of the Sunchildren, naught but shreds of the souls that once were returned at last to the Locus.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: But I still believe that, perhaps...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps...?

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: If I was the one who opened the Locus, I might be able to use my memories to supplement what remains of their souls.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Allow me to try.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Piramumon... Orupeusu... I am here. Will you not return?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did it go?

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: *sigh* Of the seven Sunchildren, Piramumon and Orupeusu were raised by mine own hand. If even they will not return...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: It seems that my memories alone are insufficient...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: If only there was something I could use as a medium... If I had the Divine Bridle, perhaps, the badge of the Sunchild's office, it might just work.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: But alas! It was lost to us long ago.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: *sigh* This nation, Byakuyakoku, still hates those children.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Perhaps my desire to free their souls is but a forlorn hope.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: ...But still, Traveler, if you would consider this my final request — could you help to find the Divine Bridle?

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: I know that the chances of finding it are quite slim, and indeed, it is rude of me to ask yet more of you.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: I... Thank you...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Still, the bridle has been lost for many long years. You need not rush.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: If you should hear of it, please, tell me.

talks.objective: Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Traveler... Have you... found the bridle?

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Could you... let me have a look at it?

talks.objective: Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Ahhh... This is the Divine Bridle. The genuine article indeed!

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: I never thought that the day would come when I might lay eyes on it once more. Traveler, tell me — whence did you get this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: From Aberaku...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: From Aberaku no Mikoto himself?

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: How strange. I remember clearly that he was a great figure from the days when our nation had just been founded.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: But it was said that he planned to usurp the seat of the Sunchild, and was branded with the crime of treason.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: But since you say that you obtained it from his hands, perhaps there are hidden things at work that I do not understand.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: So, fate has decreed the bridle should resurface here... Ah, I can recall the faces of those children already...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: This way, I might finally atone for my failings...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Traveler, place the bridle within the pool at the Locus. With it, we can surely revivify their souls.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Yes, that they may be made whole, and that they may walk the path to the next life hale!

talks.objective: Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs
Offer a Sango Pearl to the seven royal tombs
Go to the Soul Guide's Locus

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: One, two, three... Looks like we've finished paying respects at all seven tombs!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go back to the stone shrine and tell the spirit there about this.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Ah, Piramumon. You did so love books, saying that there must be a world outside our knowledge, though I did not believe you then...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: I always smiled and shook my head at your wild pronouncements. Alas, alas! I should have believed you!

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: You said that one day you would escape the Dainichi Mikoshi and venture into paths beyond...

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Go now, Piramumon. Let no one shackle you again. Go, be free!

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: And you, Orupeusu, Orupeusu. What would I give to hear you sing again?

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: There was no one who could hear your clear, pure voice, and did not wish to sing along in their hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: The night before the Rite of Solar Return, you suddenly wished to hear my voice. No matter what, you desired to hear me sing.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: You told me that no matter how terribly I sang, you would not laugh.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: You knew, didn't you? You knew that this Solar Return would be your last.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: And yet I... To the end, I...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Clymene?

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: ...I apologize, Traveler. That was unsightly of me.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: The female official who serves the Sunchildren is meant to maintain her purity... She shall never marry.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Thus, I had no children of my own all my life.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: These children, whom I served and watched grow older... At some point, they became closer to me than blood.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Thank you, Traveler. Thank you for finding the bridle.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: It has passed through the hands of every Sunchild, and the memories it has inherited are enough to fill the gaps in their souls.

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: ...Even though these memories are double-sided.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Of course. In this case, the memories are two-fold. On one hand, you have your own memories, and on the other, you have others' memories of you.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Thus the gaps are being filled by both the Sunchildren's own memories, imprinted upon the bridle...

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: As well as the memories of them as the children who were blamed by Byakuyakoku, of those who became children of sin.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: My own memories are insufficient, and so I had to supplement them with those of the people of our nation.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: And it is thanks to these transgressions that have been laid upon them that they have now been remembered by Byakuyakoku, and can now leave their afterimages behind.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Thank you, Traveler. My greatest wish now lies fulfilled.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: I can finally... be at ease.

response.speaker: Clymene
response.text: Yes, I... can finally be with those children again...

talks.objective: Place the Divine Bridle within the waters

dialogues.speaker: Clymene
dialogues.text: Please, Traveler, place the Divine Bridle within the waters of the Soul Guide's Locus...
